seeds.rationale: Camunda single-tenant mode default — the materializer must NOT auto-seed tenantIdVar from the universal prologue. When a per-scenario step seeds it (e.g. a producer like createTenant or a chained consumer that extracts the response), the seed-rules.json catch-all id rule mints a unique tenant id. When no step seeds it, ctx['tenantIdVar'] stays undefined and the consuming request omits the tenantId field, letting the REST Gateway apply the default tenant (#342). Replaces the legacy `<default>` sentinel + multipart-strip mechanism, which sent a literal sentinel on the wire and broke re-runnability for producer ops. In addition (#404), confirmed directly by the Camunda team: with multi-tenancy disabled, a FLAT optional tenantId occurrence with a non-blank value (any shape, malformed or well-formed) is always rejected with 400 and a detail containing 'multi-tenancy is disabled' — generators flip to expect that rejection instead of the field's normal behaviour. A blank/whitespace-only value is instead silently normalized to the default tenant and the request proceeds to whatever that operation's own outcome is for a tenant-omitted request (verified: 200 for simple creates, 404 for correlateMessage since no matching subscription exists) — not generalizable per-operation, so generators exclude this specific mutation class entirely rather than guess an outcome. A NESTED occurrence (e.g. a search filter field) is a different, separately-confirmed case: a malformed-but-correctly-typed STRING value is never validated, always 200 with empty results (confirmed live for constraintViolations.ts's mutations) — this does NOT extend to a wrong-TYPE value (e.g. a number or boolean), which bodyTypeMismatch.ts's mutations still correctly reject with 400 regardless of nesting, since that fails JSON deserialization before any field-level or capability check runs; bodyTypeMismatch.ts is deliberately never gated by this entry for that reason. A REQUIRED occurrence of the field name (e.g. createTenant's own tenantId, or evaluateConditionals' tenantId) is unaffected by any of this.
